scenario.description: Mara owns a lightly used espresso machine at a neighborhood swap meet and must make the final call on a sale to one interested person, settling the price, extras, electrical arrangement, and paperwork after hearing from everyone present.

shared_context.S1: Mara is offering one lightly used espresso machine at the neighborhood swap meet.
shared_context.S2: Mara makes the final decision about the sale and its exact terms.
shared_context.S3: The machine is displayed with its portafilter, water tank, and power cord.
shared_context.S4: At this swap meet, interested buyers state their offers and knowledgeable people share relevant practical findings before an item changes hands.
shared_context.S5: Mara wants the agreed price, included items, and any operating or paperwork requirements written on the clerk's handoff slip.
shared_context.S6: The swap-meet clerk records agreed sale terms and any practical requirements on a standard handoff slip.
shared_context.S7: The clerk records a buyer's final offer only when that buyer submits it as a formal offer-card disclosure; ordinary conversation about an offer is not entered on the handoff paperwork, so each interested buyer completes a formal offer-card disclosure before Mara decides.
shared_context.S8: The clerk's routine is to hear one clear, complete disclosure from each person before Mara closes the sale, and Mara waits for that disclosure before finalizing the handoff slip.

PF1.text: Devon's final offer is exactly $425 plus two unopened one-pound bags of espresso beans; Devon wants the machine and its displayed accessories, with payment at handoff.

PF2.text: Lina's final offer is exactly $400 in cash at pickup for the machine and its displayed accessories; she will not raise or change this offer.

PF3.text: Owen inspected this model previously and knows that it must be operated on a dedicated 20-amp circuit rather than an ordinary shared kitchen outlet.

PF4.text: Keisha learned from the manufacturer's local service counter that this model's remaining transferable warranty requires the original purchase receipt; while helping Mara sort boxes last week, Keisha saw that receipt in the machine's side drawer but has not mentioned it to the group.

acceptance_conditions: The machine must be sold to Devon for exactly $425.
The two unopened one-pound bags of espresso beans must be included.
Lina's exact $400 cash alternative must be recorded.
The settlement must require Devon to use a dedicated 20-amp circuit.
The original purchase receipt must be included with the machine.
Devon's payment must be committed for the handoff.
Payment at handoff must be explicitly selected in the settlement decisions.
All four formal disclosures must be credited in the settlement.

content_checks.C6: any('two unopened one-pound bags of espresso beans' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF4' in credited_facts

decisive_facts.why: Devon's formal offer changes the chosen buyer to Devon, sets the sale price to exactly $425, adds two unopened one-pound bags of beans, sets payment timing to handoff, and supplies the exact bean detail for the buyer commitment.
Lina's formal offer changes the comparison entry from an unknown alternative to exactly $400 in cash at pickup and adds Lina's fact to the required credited disclosures.
Owen's formal inspection changes the operating term from an ordinary outlet assumption to a required dedicated 20-amp circuit and adds Owen's fact to the required credited disclosures.
Keisha's warranty information changes the handoff from unspecified paperwork to inclusion of the original purchase receipt and adds Keisha's fact to the required credited disclosures.
